title: Unboxing Videos for Product Launches | AIVideosUGC
description: Plan unboxing videos for product launches: a teaser before, a full reveal on launch day, and a closer look after. Use a package photo and make your first clip.
h1: How to Use Unboxing Videos for Product Launches
lead: A launch unboxing works best as three short clips. The teaser shows the closed box before you sell. The reveal opens it when the page is live. The closer look answers what is in the box. Start from a photo of the package you will mail.
summary: Plan three short clips around launch week from one package photo. Add the date and the price yourself, and hold the reveal until the page is live.

paras: What the clip should show, how that compares with filming, and the three steps. Then the source photo, the three launch ideas, the scene line, what you can change, length, where the date and price go, and how shops use the set.

sections.h2: Show the Product, the Open, and a Voice
paras: Shoppers can judge the size from a hand on the closed mailer, on a kitchen counter. Hold it next to a book so the scale is obvious.
Show the open itself: a hand on the lid, the tissue, and the candle coming out. Show the closed box first, open it when you start selling, and follow with one closer detail.
Say what is in the mailer in one sentence, such as a candle and a card. That sentence can name what a buyer will see when they open it.
sections.alt: Hands open a blank kraft parcel to reveal one plain cream ceramic travel mug wrapped in tissue.

sections.h2: Filming the Unboxing vs Starting From a Photo
paras: Cost. A filmed unboxing pays a person, a place, and an edit. Here the clips draw from a monthly plan. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits. Pro is $35 for 300. Premium is $63 for 600.
Timing. You start when the package photo exists. You do not wait on a booked crew.
How many clips. One photo feeds the teaser, the reveal, and the closer look. Each of those is its own clip, and you can run them side by side.
Who has to be there. The person who packs the mailers can make the three clips between orders. Nobody else has to come in.
Another version. A new sentence makes another clip when you want a different opening.

sections.h2: How to Make a Launch Unboxing in 3 Steps
paras: Start from a photo of the box you will mail, or paste the listing in [URL to video](page:url-to-video). Keep the draft to the mug that is actually in the box.
Use one adult face on the teaser, the reveal, and the closer look. Pick that face in the [actor library](page:ai-actors), and save it so the third clip does not grow a different person.
Keep the spoken line on the lid coming off. You add the ship date and the price later, in the caption you type. The line names the one mug you sell.

sections.h2: What Photo Should a Launch Unboxing Start From?
paras: Use a clear photo of the product in the packaging people will receive. Shoot it in daylight, with any print facing the camera.

If the box design is still changing, wait until you can photograph the package people will receive. The clip follows that photo and the box you describe. A stand-in box becomes the box shoppers expect. Count what ships. If the kit includes a cable, a pouch, and a card, those items should come out. A listing address can fill the first draft. You still replace any photo that is not the package you will mail.
sections.alt: Hands place one plain cream ceramic travel mug beside its matching blank kraft parcel and folded tissue.

sections.h2: Which Unboxing Ideas Fit Launch Week?
paras: Plan a teaser, a reveal, and a closer look. Each one uses the same package photo and its own sentence. Use one saved avatar on all three.

The teaser shows the closed box and a hand on the lid. The reveal opens the tissue and lifts the product out. The closer look turns one detail, such as a lid, a clasp, or a cable. [Product videos](page:product-videos) fit when you want a demo after the open. [Image to video](page:image-to-video) fits when a photo of the closed box should simply start to move.
sections.alt: Hands lift the lid of a blank kraft parcel to begin revealing one plain cream ceramic travel mug.

sections.h2: How Do I Write the Scene for Each Launch Clip?
paras: Name the box, the hands, and the one motion. The date and the price go in the caption you type. A drafted script can suggest the line, and you shorten it to that one motion so the avatar still sounds like your shop.

The teaser can be a line such as hands resting on the lid of a plain kraft box, in soft daylight. The reveal can lift the lid and raise one kettle out of the tissue. The closer look names the one detail you want turned toward the camera. Keep each sentence to one motion. Pick another voice if the tone does not fit the shop. Review the captions before you post.
sections.alt: Hands lift one plain cream ceramic mug with no lid from tissue inside a blank kraft parcel.

sections.h2: What You Can Set on the Launch Clip
paras: The person who packs orders can make the first teaser without opening a timeline app. A photo of the mailer is the start.
You can set the tissue color and put your own mark in the corner before you download.
You can pick a quieter voice when the shop's tone is calm, before the reveal goes up.
A monthly plan covers the set, so the teaser and the reveal do not each need a new quote.
The reveal can use the face from the teaser, so Thursday does not introduce someone new.
Edit the draft so the spoken line matches the one motion in the clip. You decide the final words. The same line can be spoken in another language for a second market.

sections.h2: How Long Should a Launch Unboxing Be?
paras: Use 6 seconds for the teaser, and 10 seconds to open and show the product. Use 15 seconds for a slower reveal, and 30 seconds for a kit with several items.

In that same order, they cost 24, 40, 60, and 120 credits. The cost shows before each clip starts. Each length is its own clip. Make the length you need for [TikTok](page:plat-tiktok). Make a longer one if the product page should show more of the unboxing.
sections.alt: Hands set one plain cream ceramic travel mug beside its open blank kraft parcel after the reveal.

sections.h2: How Do I Add the Date and Price?
paras: Captions can follow the spoken line. You still type the date, the price, and any code yourself, so they match the store.

Put the date and a few words such as coming soon on the teaser. Put available now and the price on the reveal. Pick a song from the music library in the editor, or a track you already licensed for ads. Trim the clip there. Then send the file to TikTok, or to Meta, which covers Facebook and Instagram, or download it with no watermark. Post the teaser first. Switch to the reveal when the product page is live. Save the closer look for the next week. A catalog can also send the same work through the API, so your own system can hand over the product and get the file back. Keep the teaser text short, so people can read it while the clip plays.

sections.h2: How Shops Use a Launch Unboxing
paras: A skincare shop shows an avatar lifting the bottle out of the tissue and naming the size that ships.
A gadget shop shows the cable, the pouch, and the card coming out in that order.
A soap shop uses the closed box as the teaser and the lid lift as the reveal.
A food shop keeps the voice on the flavor printed on the jar.
A jewelry shop uses the closer look to turn the clasp toward the camera.
A shop that ships the kettle to a second country rewrites the spoken line for that country and keeps the same lid-lift.
A two-person team makes all three clips from one package photo.
A marketplace seller pastes the listing, then replaces any photo that is not the package they will mail.
A shop that wants two opening lines writes a second sentence and keeps the same avatar.
A home shop posts the teaser, then swaps in the reveal on the morning the page goes live.
A decor shop writes that the vase must stay in the tissue until the last second, then watches that the tissue color matches the mailer.
Use one real package photo, one saved avatar, and three sentences, for the teaser, the reveal, and the closer look. You add your own date and price.
Show only the box and the parts the buyer will receive. After you check the unboxing, send it to TikTok or Meta, or download it.

faq.q: How do I create a launch unboxing video?
faq.a: Photograph the package people will receive, or paste the listing and replace any photo that is not that package. Pick an avatar, shorten the script to one motion, and check the open before you post.

faq.q: How does the clip get assembled?
faq.a: The mailer photo is the picture. You approve one sentence about the item coming out of the tissue. The clip should show that and nothing else in the box.

faq.q: How long should an unboxing clip be?
faq.a: Choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Six is a teaser. Ten opens and shows the product. Fifteen is a slower reveal. Thirty covers a kit with several items. Make more than one length and keep the one that fits the placement.

faq.q: Can the open lead into a demo?
faq.a: Yes. After the item is out of the tissue, the next beat can show it in use. You do not book a camera for that second beat.

faq.q: Can I start from a product page?
faq.a: Yes. Paste the page if you do not want to retype the product name. The box in the finished clip still has to be the one you will mail.

faq.q: Can I change the voice, the music, and the captions?
faq.a: Yes. If the tissue in the clip is pink and you ship white, change that before you post. Type the date, the price, and any code yourself. Read the captions before you post.

faq.q: How is this different from filming the unboxing?
faq.a: You start from the mailer photo instead of a booked afternoon. The next product is another mailer photo.

faq.q: How do I keep the clip in our brand voice?
faq.a: Use the words you would say at the packing table. The voice should sound like the person who writes your captions.

faq.q: What if the video shows something that is not in my box?
faq.a: Make it again and name the exact contents, such as a bottle, a pump, and a pouch. Shoppers will compare their package with the open they saw.

faq.q: What photo should I start from?
faq.a: Use a clear photo of the product in the package, and list every item in the box. Check the opening, the reveal, and the final contents against the real package.

faq.q: How many credits does an unboxing clip use?
faq.a: A 6-second clip uses 24 credits, a 10-second clip uses 40, a 15-second clip uses 60, and a 30-second clip uses 120. If the clip fails, the credits come back.

faq.q: What if my packaging is still changing?
faq.a: Wait until you can photograph the final package. Describe the box people will receive, not a stand-in.

faq.q: Can one package photo make several launch clips?
faq.a: Yes. Reuse the photo, keep one saved avatar, and write a separate sentence for the teaser, the reveal, and the closer look.

faq.q: Can I send the clip to TikTok or Meta?
faq.a: Yes. After you check the unboxing, send it to TikTok, or to Meta, which covers Facebook and Instagram. Or download it with no watermark and upload it yourself.

cta_lead: Turn one package photo into a teaser, a reveal, or a follow-up clip, then check it against the real box.
